## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## honeycomb
Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). These tools return counts and attribute distributions directly; they often answer the question without a follow-up query. Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1. ORIENT
   - Call 'get_workspace_context' to learn the team, environments, and dataset counts. Use the returned environment slug in subsequent calls.

2. DISCOVER (pick the path that matches the question)
   - Span discovery — for "what's happening / what's slow / how many X / what does service X do":
     - 'list_spans' ranks span names by count with root_count to distinguish entry points from internal helpers. Counts here are often the answer to "how many X happened".
     - 'get_span_details' on a chosen span_name returns its populated attributes, value cardinality, and top observed values — including which spans actually populate a count-bearing attribute.
     Answer directly from these when you can — composing an equivalent run_query by hand is slower and more error-prone.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. 138	func renderExperimentalCommands(commands []experimentalCommandInfo) string {
139		width := 0
140		for _, info := range commands {
141			if w := utf8.RuneCountInString(info.Invocation); w > width {
142				width = w
143			}
144		}
145	
146		var out strings.Builder
147		for _, info := range commands {
148			out.WriteString("  ")
149			out.WriteString(padRight(info.Invocation, width))
150			out.WriteByte(' ')
151			out.WriteString(info.Summary)
152			out.WriteByte('\n')
153		}
154		return out.String()
155	}
156	
157	func padRight(value string, width int) string {
158		n := utf8.RuneCountInString(value)
159		if n >= width {
160			return value
161		}
162		return value + strings.Repeat(" ", width-n)
163	}

  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
  `adopt` moves an active session from another repo or worktree into the current
  worktree and resets target-local checkpoint bookkeeping so future commits link
  to the adopted session from the new location.
- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`, plus
  the deprecated `rewind` (functional, prints a cobra deprecation message, will
  be removed in a future release)
- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`, plus
  `token` (prints the active control-plane bearer to stdout for scripting/curl;
  honors `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, else the refreshed active-context login JWT). `token`
  also takes `--jurisdiction <slug>` (e.g. `us`, `eu`), which instead mints a
  jurisdictional identity token (RFC 8693 exchange, `scope=openid`,
  `aud=<jurisdiction host>`) for that jurisdiction's entire-api cells (e.g.
  `https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io/api/v1`), which reject the control-plane
  bearer; it exchanges `ENTIRE_TOKEN` when set (deriving the environment from the
  env token's `aud`), else the active login. `auth status` shows the caller's
  home jurisdiction so the slug is discoverable. `logout`
  takes `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`

Experimental command families advertised through `entire labs`:

- `tokens`: `profile` (hidden from root help while token diagnostics mature)

Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
`configure`, `agent-help`, `api`.
